title: bring a document back in line with the code
display: docs back in line with the code
about: One narrow job written out: a document claims things the code no longer does, and this is the shape of putting that right. It is here as a worked example of what a template IS — steps of your own, plus `merge` named from the library so its review comes along — and not as the shape a job takes. Most jobs look nothing like this one. Take it when the job is this job, and write your own steps when it is not. The `after` on each step is its place in the order: entry numbers, 1-based, and what the board draws the arrows from.

steps.name: list every claim the document makes about the code
check each claim against the code; write down which have drifted and how
rewrite what drifted, and cut what the code no longer does at all
run every example and command the document gives

notes: Copied from the `docs` template. Add, drop and reshape steps as the job turns out — nothing links this plan back to what it came from.
